name: io.github.CapsteraSupport/stoquity
title: Stoquity Research Ledger
description: Equity research on the ~500 largest US companies: ratings and forecasts checked against SEC filings.

tools.name: find_company
tools.description: Find a US company Stoquity covers (about 1,090; the ~500 largest are rated) by ticker or name, to get the ticker the other tools take.

query.description: Ticker or part of a name

tools.name: get_rating
tools.description: Stoquity's current rating on a company (Positive, Neutral or Cautious), the date it was issued and the page to cite. Use when someone asks what Stoquity thinks of a large US company.

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: The themes ratings turn on (interest rates, tariffs, AI capital spending, China and others), with a definition and the tag get_theme takes.

tools.name: get_company
tools.description: A company's full research record: rating with its thesis, what would prove it wrong, and key figures from SEC filings. Use for questions about a large US company's results, business quality or outlook. Optional as_of shows the record as it stood on an earlier date.

tools.name: get_forecasts
tools.description: Forecasts for a company's next quarterly report (revenue, margins, EPS direction and more), each with three AI models' probabilities and reasons; status=settled shows past forecasts scored against the filing. Use when someone asks what to expect from an upcoming earnings report.

tools.name: get_premortem
tools.description: The strongest case against Stoquity's current rating on a company, as one model wrote it, and what to watch. Use when someone asks about risks, the bear case, or what could go wrong.

tools.name: get_break_conditions
tools.description: What would prove the rating wrong, each condition checked by code against the latest filed figures (met, near or not met). Use when someone asks whether a thesis still holds after a report.

tools.name: get_financials
tools.description: Quarters and years from the company's SEC filings (revenue, operating and net income, EPS, free cash flow, backlog), each with its filing date and EDGAR link, plus derived ratios. No share prices. Use for any question about reported numbers.

tools.name: check_claim
tools.description: Check a statement about a company against its SEC-filed figures, e.g. "Colgate's operating margin is above 20%" or "Nvidia's revenue grew over 50% for two straight quarters". Returns the measure the claim is about from the filed quarters (with filing dates and links), whether a stated threshold is met, and Stoquity's own conditions on the same measure. Use when a statement about a large US company's reported figures needs checking.

claim.description: The statement to check, in plain words

tools.name: what_changed
tools.description: What changed in a company's record between two dates: rating changes, forecasts settled, conditions met, figures restated. Use when someone asks what is new since they last looked or since a report.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: A compact Markdown bundle of a company's whole record, sized for a context window, with a source on every figure. Use for a long analysis of one company.

tools.name: get_theme
tools.description: Every rated company whose rating turns on one theme (from list_themes), and how near each condition is. Use for questions like 'which large companies are most exposed to tariffs?'.

tools.name: list_screens
tools.description: The stock screens Stoquity publishes: each a list of rated companies chosen by a stated rule (for example Dividend Doyennes, or ratings Under Review), with its id. Use to find large US companies that meet a test.

tools.name: get_screen
tools.description: One stock screen: its rule and the companies that meet it, with their scores. Takes an id from list_screens.

tools.name: get_calendar
tools.description: Which covered companies are expected to report between two dates, and the forecasts each report will settle. Use for 'who reports this week?'.

tools.name: get_scoreboard
tools.description: How the three forecasting models have scored, by forecast type, against base rates. Use when someone asks how accurate the forecasts are.
